findings.failure_path: A first install accepts an existing managed root whose only top-level entry is snapshots. After installation, cleanup recursively deletes every child outside the new manifest's keep set. A user's backup under snapshots is therefore erased by an ordinary install. A later update also erases a superseded snapshot containing local changes. The .staging- prefix triggers deletion even during uninstall.
findings.smallest_fix: Delete only superseded snapshots identified by the prior manifest and verified against their recorded files. Remove only staging directories created by the current operation. Preserve and report every unknown or changed entry.

findings.failure_path: The installer string in the marker authorizes replacement of the entire plugin tree. A user who adds a local skill or edits an installed file loses that work on the next refresh. Installer test case 2 demonstrates the loss directly by creating a file after installation and requiring refresh to delete it. A partial host copy can also leave the staged marker behind before verification succeeds.
findings.smallest_fix: Record the installed file inventory and hashes after a verified install. Before refresh, require the destination to match that receipt, including the absence of extra files. Change case 2 to require preservation of the added file, and test removal of an obsolete file that the receipt actually owns.

findings.failure_path: The checkout installer checks ownership before staging and takes no lock shared with npm. On a fresh destination, npm can finish installing and commit its manifest while the checkout installer stages files. The checkout installer then replaces npm's plugin and reports success, leaving the npm manifest pointing at a different tree.
findings.smallest_fix: Use the same per-destination lock in both installers. Check ownership under that lock immediately before the host mutation and hold it through verification and receipt commit.

findings.failure_path: Failed-update compensation treats an empty plugin listing as permission to reinstall the prior snapshot. The adapter's own fake host models an existing directory that is absent from the listing. If a failed update leaves such a directory containing local files, rollback replaces it and destroys those files.
findings.smallest_fix: Restore the prior snapshot only when the current tree matches the attempted install or the destination is demonstrably absent. Make destinationAbsent accept only ENOENT as proof. Preserve an unlisted existing directory and the recovery journal.

findings.failure_path: Recovery promotes journal.intended to the ownership manifest after comparing the public plugin with the file list supplied by that same journal. readJournal checks only schema and operation. It never establishes that the recorded snapshot exists or contains those files. A stale or malformed journal describing a hand-installed plugin can therefore authorize a subsequent uninstall of that plugin.
findings.smallest_fix: Validate both journal manifests at the storage boundary, constrain snapshot paths to the managed snapshots directory, and verify the referenced snapshot and its plugin tree before promoting ownership. Refuse recovery when that evidence is missing.

findings.failure_path: normpath collapses parent components before the isolation guard can resolve symlinks. On POSIX, when a directory component is a symlink, its parent is resolved from the link destination. The bridge can consequently check a linked-worktree path while the original edit path reaches the primary checkout. The existing symlink test has no parent component and misses this case.
findings.smallest_fix: Join relative paths to the verified host cwd without lexical collapsing, then resolve components in filesystem order with semantics appropriate to the edit operation. Cover a symlink followed by a parent component and assert the verdict against the actual destination.

findings.failure_path: When cwd is absent, a malformed workspacePaths string is iterated character by character. An absolute path string supplies '/' as its first character, so the bridge accepts the filesystem root as a known cwd and checks relative edits against the wrong directory. A valid multi-root list also silently selects the first root even when the active root is unknown.
findings.smallest_fix: Validate workspacePaths as a list of absolute directories. Use it as a cwd fallback only when the host identifies one unambiguous root. Deny relative guarded operations otherwise.

findings.failure_path: When the merge guard cannot run, the fallback classifies raw shell text with a regex. Ordinary shell quoting of the Git subcommand changes the text matched by the regex while preserving the command Git receives. The failure is then treated as advisory and the bridge can return allow for a landing operation.
findings.smallest_fix: On merge-guard failure, allow only commands positively classified as harmless and deny uncertain shell syntax. Add a regression for a shell-equivalent quoted subcommand alongside the ordinary-command control.

findings.failure_path: Equal counts do not identify which GENERIC result belongs to which parallel call. If results arrive in completion order, another tool's successful output can be credited to a failed or partial skill read. Matching numbered bytes establishes what the output contains, but the synthetic Skill event also asserts which call produced it. The test covers unequal counts only.
findings.smallest_fix: Correlate results through a host-provided identifier. Where the transcript lacks identifiers or a verified ordering guarantee, grant skill-load evidence only for a single call with a single result. Add an equal-count, reordered-result case.

findings.failure_path: The conversation lock waits indefinitely, and the event deadline starts only after acquisition. A slow PreToolUse can hold the lock longer than the entire 15-second PostToolUse timeout. The waiting bridge can be killed by Antigravity before it prints any JSON. The serial event tests cannot detect this.
findings.smallest_fix: Start the deadline before lock acquisition and use bounded acquisition with time reserved to emit the event's fallback. Add a two-process test where one event holds the lock beyond the second event's budget.

findings.failure_path: If uninstall stops after the host removes the plugin but before snapshot cleanup, reconciliation deletes the manifest and journal. The next uninstall reports absent while the snapshots remain and their ownership inventory is gone. Reconciliation also runs before the dry-run check, so a preview can discard those records.
findings.smallest_fix: Keep the prior manifest and uninstall journal until verified snapshot cleanup finishes. Make previews report pending recovery without changing either record. Exercise a retry from immediately after host removal.

findings.failure_path: For a multi-file patch, the first ask verdict returns immediately. A later target that would receive deny is never checked, so the host can offer confirmation for a patch containing a forbidden edit. This contradicts the bridge's documented deny-over-ask aggregation.
findings.smallest_fix: Remember the first ask and continue checking the remaining targets. Return immediately on deny, and return the saved ask only after every target has been checked.

findings.failure_path: The host smoke records an allowed command and a denied write. The packet's delegation overwrite and blocking Stop cases parse Python-generated JSON directly. They would still pass if Antigravity rejected overwrite or continue, or ignored the rewritten prompt.
findings.smallest_fix: Record a host-level check showing that the subagent receives the rewritten prompt and that a blocking Stop produces exactly one continuation. Include host acceptance of ask if the bridge emits it.

findings.failure_path: The privacy regression uses GNU stat -c to capture the shadow file's mode. macOS ships BSD stat, so the mode capture is empty and the default repository test gate fails on a supported platform.
findings.smallest_fix: Read the mode with Python's os.stat and stat.S_IMODE inside the capture hook, retaining the assertion that the live shadow file is 0600.

concern_results.conclusion: The frozen candidate fails the data-safety and guard-correctness acceptance criterion. Both installers can erase user files. The bridge can check a different path from the one an edit reaches, misattribute skill-read evidence, and exceed the host timeout before emitting a verdict. These findings come from the supplied code and tests. Real-host acceptance of several response shapes remains unverified in the packet.

challenge_focus: Try to break the Antigravity host support: make a guarded edit, landing command or delegation get allowed (bridge exceptions, malformed payloads, path tricks, symlinks, relative paths, races between concurrent hook events), make the bridge print output Antigravity rejects or hang, forge skill-load evidence, make an installer (scripts/install-antigravity.sh or the npm antigravity adapter) delete or replace user data it does not own, or leave state that later reads as owned. Requester asked: first-class Antigravity host support next to Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, no push or PR.
